colophon: Abirami Antati, graciously composed by Abirami Bhattar.

lines.1: O son of Uma, who is one half of the Lord of Thillai who wears garlands of konrai and shenbaga flowers,
lines.2: you who pervade all seven worlds —
lines.3: may this glorious Abirami Antati ever dwell within my mind,
lines.4: O dark-bodied Ganapati, stand by me as I compose these words.
lines.5: Like the rising red sun, like the sacred mark upon the brow,
lines.6: like the ruby that the wise prize, like a pomegranate bud, like a lotus in bloom,
lines.7: like a flash of praised lightning, like the soft, fragrant red of kumkum paste —
lines.8: such is the radiant form fate has fashioned for Abirami; she alone is my true refuge.
lines.9: She is my refuge, the very god I worship, the mother who bore me, and she who is the trunk, the tender shoot, and the deep root of the Vedas,
lines.10: holding in her hands the arrow of fresh flowers, the sugarcane bow, and the soft goose-driving hook —
lines.12: it is she who is Tripura Sundari.
lines.13: I have come to know the Veda that no one else truly knows; and having known it,
lines.14: I have drawn close to your sacred feet alone, O Goddess of fortune —
lines.15: and in fear I have turned away from those hard-hearted men who do not weigh the greatness of your devotees,
lines.16: men who, stumbling, fall into the hell that awaits them.
lines.17: Men, gods, and sages of illusion-conquering power all come and bow their heads
lines.19: and he who bears upon his long matted locks the cool moon, the serpent, and the river Ganga,
lines.20: that holy one, and you together — may you both dwell in my mind forever.
lines.21: She who is the perfect Tripura, whose full, close-set breasts speak their own eloquence,
lines.22: the jewel of the mind, whose waist is slender as a creeper worn thin —
lines.23: the Mother who turned the poison the long-matted one drank into nectar,
lines.24: the flawless Sundari, the formless Andhari — her feet alone rest upon my head.
lines.25: Upon my head rests your golden lotus feet; within my heart
lines.26: abides forever your sacred mantra, O woman hued like vermilion —
lines.27: joined always with your devotees, in due and proper order,
lines.28: what I have composed, again and again, is nothing but your own supreme Agama scripture.
lines.29: My soul churns like the staff endlessly stirring curdling milk;
lines.30: consider it, and grant it an unfailing path of grace.
lines.31: Brahma of the lotus-seat, and he who delights wearing the crescent moon on his crown, and Vishnu — all bow
lines.32: in constant praise before your feet, O beautiful, vermilion-faced Sundari.
lines.33: Sundari, my father's consort — may she come and, with her vermilion form, tear away all the bonds of my worldly attachment;
lines.34: she who once stood upon the head of the buffalo-demon,
lines.35: the boundless one, the dark-blue one, the ever-unfading Virgin, whom the Vedas seek —
lines.36: her flower-soft hand, held in the hand of the Lord who bears the Vedas, alone fills my thought.
lines.37: Dark and deep are the eyes of my father Shiva, and vast, like the golden mountain, are
lines.38: your breasts, which nourished the child who cried for milk, granting it your great compassionate grace;
lines.39: lovely too are the ornaments and garlands you wear, the sugarcane bow and arrow in your red hand,
lines.40: and your bud-like smile — may you, O Mother, come and stand before me, together with all of these.
lines.41: Standing, sitting, lying down, or walking — it is you alone I think of;
lines.42: always it is your flower-feet that I worship — O rare treasure that is the very meaning distilled from the four Vedas,
lines.43: O grace itself, O Uma, you who long ago were born
lines.44: of the Himalayas, O bliss of eternal, undying liberation!
lines.45: As bliss, as my own awareness, as nectar filling all things,
lines.46: she whose form is boundless as the sky, she who is the final goal even of the four Vedas —
lines.47: her lotus feet, that final goal, rest as an ornament on the matted crown
lines.48: of my Lord, whose white dance-ground is the cremation forest.
lines.49: What I have chosen to cherish is your glory; what I have learned by heart is your name; melting with devotion,
lines.50: what I have composed is offered at your two lotus feet; day and night
lines.51: what I have drawn near to is the company of those who love you — what merit did I ever perform before,
lines.52: to deserve this, O Mother, who has brought all seven worlds into bloom?
lines.53: You who brought all fourteen worlds into bloom, and having brought them forth,
lines.54: you who protect them, and you who then withdraw them again — you who are elder
lines.55: to the blue-throated Lord, yet younger sister to the ever-undying Mukunda,
lines.56: you who are the great ascetic — is there any other god worth worshipping besides you?
lines.57: Those who worship you are the gods and the demons alike; those who meditate on you
lines.58: are the four-faced Brahma and Narayana; those who hold you bound
lines.59: within their hearts are the undying ones of supreme bliss, the liberated —
lines.60: yet to reach you on this earth is made easy, even for the humblest, O my Queen, by your own compassion.
lines.61: Those who once performed crores of penances seeking your grace —
lines.62: would they be content merely to obtain earthly wealth?
lines.63: Surely they win the wealth the gods enjoy in heaven, and beyond that, undying liberation itself —
lines.64: O fragrant, dark-green parrot, whose very speech is music!
lines.65: O parrot! O light that lies within the hearts of your kinsmen and blazes forth,
lines.66: O source of all light, O the very space in which numberless things have no reckoning,
lines.67: O vast emptiness, O Mother who, beginning from that void, expanded into the five elements —
lines.68: wonder of wonders: you remain beyond the small measure of this poor mind's understanding.
lines.69: She of wondrous form, whose lotus-like face all the lotuses of the world seem to praise,
lines.70: Sundaravalli, the very equal in loveliness of Rati, wife of Kama —
lines.71: seeing her beauty, was it not to the wonderment of all who once witnessed it
lines.72: that he took her, that union once thought impossible, as the left half of his own body?
lines.73: May the gracious beauty of the Lord who took you as half of his form, and you together,
lines.74: and the splendour of your sacred wedded union, remain fixed within my heart —
lines.75: and may your golden feet, which cleared away all impurity from me and took me as your own,
lines.76: come and stand visibly before me, when the fierce god of death approaches me.
lines.77: Gazing upon your sacred form standing manifest before me, my eyes and my heart
lines.78: have found no shore to the flood of rapture that has risen in me;
lines.79: yet within my mind a clear wisdom now shines forth — what can this be, what is your sacred will,
lines.80: O you who dwell pervading all nine luminous corners of the mystic diagram?
lines.81: Where is your true temple in which you dwell — is it beside your Lord,
lines.82: or is it in the foot or the crown of the four resounding Vedas, or is it
lines.83: the white moon brimming with nectar, or the lotus, or is it this heart of mine,
lines.84: or the ocean where all things disappear? O auspicious one of the perfect mountain!
lines.85: Auspicious one, whose breasts are like full pitchers, daughter of the mountain, who holds in her red hand
lines.86: the conch that resounds from the ocean, mistress of every art, beside whom the Ganga leaps —
lines.87: she who stands at the side of him whose thick, piled matted hair holds back the surging river,
lines.88: she who is tawny, dark-blue, red, and fair by turns — O tender golden creeper of a woman!
lines.89: O creeper, O tender branch of the vanji tree, O ripe fruit that has fallen freely for me,
lines.90: O fragrance distilled from the Vedas, O young she-elephant of the great snowy Himalayas,
lines.91: O Mother who gave birth even to Brahma and the other gods —
lines.92: this servant of yours — let me die here, and come take me as your own, that I be never born again.
lines.93: I hold nothing in my mind but your beauty; I will never abandon the company of your devotees;
lines.94: I will never desire another faith; you who dwell within the vast three worlds
lines.95: and yet stand beyond all things — you, the toddy that has fermented within my very heart,
lines.96: the intoxication of that toddy itself — O tender one, O the very pupil of my eye!
lines.97: O jewel, O radiance of the jewel, O the very ornament set with that shining gem,
lines.98: O beauty that adorns even the ornament — to those who do not draw near you, you are
lines.99: sickness itself, yet to your own you are the cure for sickness, the great feast of the immortals —
lines.100: once I have bowed at your lotus feet, I shall bow to no one else.
lines.101: Following behind, cherishing your devotees, that my cycle of births might be cut off,
lines.102: I strove in penance before all this — O elder sister to the first three gods,
lines.103: O Mother, O rare medicine for this whole world, known as Abirami —
lines.104: what then? — from now I shall stand and praise you forever, never forgetting you.
lines.105: Your devotees who praise you become themselves creators, sustainers, and destroyers
lines.106: of all fourteen worlds — O divine one who wears the fragrant kadamba flower in your hair!
lines.107: That my poor tongue's clumsy words should have risen to reach your fragrant, twin feet
lines.108: is itself a wonder worth laughing at.
lines.109: You have shattered my deceitful cycle of births; you have created in me
lines.110: a heart that melts with love; you have entrusted to me alone the sacred duty of wearing your lotus feet upon my head;
lines.111: with the flood-waters of your grace you have washed away
lines.112: every impurity of my heart — Sundari, how then can I ever describe your grace?
lines.113: As word and its meaning, joined with your dancing consort, you stand as one —
lines.114: O fragrant flowering creeper! For those who worship your fresh lotus feet
lines.115: night and day, an undying kingdom of grace,
lines.116: the true path of penance, and even the world of Shiva itself will surely be attained.
lines.117: You are the attainment itself, and the goddess who bestows that attainment, shining as the supreme
lines.118: Power, and the Auspicious One in whom that Power flourishes; you are the liberation that ascetics strive for,
lines.119: and the seed of that liberation, and the very intelligence that sprouts and grows from that seed,
lines.120: and, within that intelligence, the city of consciousness which you yourself protect.
lines.121: Long ago you stopped and claimed me as your own — was that not, then, already a bond you took on?
lines.122: What good is it now to you? Whatever I do from here, even should I
lines.123: fall and sink into the very middle of the raging sea, is it not still your sacred will to bring me safe to shore?
lines.124: O you who are the One, yet the many forms, yet the formless — my own Uma!
lines.125: Uma and the one who holds her as half of his own form, having come together in a single shape,
lines.126: have made even us capable of loving them; now there remains nothing further to weigh or reckon —
lines.127: no mother who gave birth ever gave more, for there is no other refuge;
lines.128: all that is left is the longing I have set upon her of the perfect, bamboo-slender shoulders.
lines.129: Caught in the ocean of desire, suffering in the merciless noose of death,
lines.130: you took your fragrant lotus feet and firmly placed them upon my head,
lines.131: and claimed me as your own —
lines.132: how can I ever put into words that love, O jewel of a woman who is half of the Lord's body?
lines.133: When Death, who pursues us according to the deeds we have woven, comes to summon me,
lines.134: and I tremble, may you come and say 'fear not' —
lines.135: O tender dark one, whose sandal-anointed, full breasts melt even the Lord's own heart —
lines.136: in that hour of anguish, I shall run to you alone, crying 'Mother!'
lines.137: To devotees who come seeking refuge in you, four-faced Brahma himself lovingly gives heaven
lines.139: you are the great bejewelled body and the half of the Lord that hosts it, the golden lotus flower dripping fresh honey,
lines.140: the blazing sun, and the moon.
lines.141: That your small, fragrant feet, sweet as the crescent moon, should rest upon my head —
lines.142: what penance of mine could ever have earned me this? Not even the countless gods of heaven,
lines.143: nor he who sleeps upon the cool serpent-bed amid the billowing ocean,
lines.144: O precious treasure — could any of them attain such fortune?
lines.145: You are wealth itself, and the enjoyment that wealth brings; you are the bewildering delusion that grants that rare enjoyment,
lines.146: and the clear wisdom that arises even out of delusion — within the deceit of my own mind,
lines.147: without any darkness at all, your grace remains as pure, boundless light —
lines.148: yet what that grace of yours truly is, I do not know, O Ambika seated on the lotus!
lines.149: For her hands, her only ornament is sugarcane and flowers; for her lotus-like body,
lines.150: her only ornament is a string of white pearls; for the hood of the poisonous serpent she wears,
lines.151: her ornament is a string of many gems, and silk —
lines.152: she alone belongs beside him whose glory adorns all eight directions.
lines.153: With her red lips ripened like fruit on a coral vine, and her cool, white,
lines.154: gracious smile as her only weapons, she wages a gentle contest
lines.155: with our own Shankara himself, her twin breasts bending her slender, hourglass waist —
lines.156: bow to her, I tell you, if you wish to rule even the heaven of Amaravati!
lines.157: To rule my life, I have your lotus feet; to be freed from the grip of Death,
lines.158: I have the corner of your glance; and if these graces should ever fail to reach fullness in me,
lines.159: the fault is not mine, but yours — O bright-browed one, seated as the half
lines.160: of him who strung his bow and loosed the arrow that burned down the three cities!
lines.161: The bright-browed Virgin, whom all the gods come and worship, longing to hold her dear,
lines.162: our own Queen, the Virgin who to a foolish heart can seem
lines.163: unreachable, hard to behold — that I should conceive the very thought of wearing love for her, of seeing her,
lines.164: is that not itself the fruit of merit I performed in a former life?
lines.165: We have indeed performed merit, O my mind! — that the fresh blue-lily-eyed Virgin
lines.166: and her radiant Lord, coming together for our sake,
lines.167: should draw near and come here, standing among their own devotees,
lines.168: and plant their lotus feet firmly upon our heads.
lines.169: Swelling to fill all space, pressed close together, soft yet firm, strung with pearls —
lines.170: her breast-mountains conquered even the unyielding heart of the Lord;
lines.171: the Queen whose very nature is the dance, whose hips are curved like the hood of the cobra,
lines.172: whose speech is cool as frost — she who wears the anklets that echo the sacred Veda!
lines.173: Her small anklet-ringed feet hold the noose and the goad; her hands hold the five flower-arrows; her speech is sweet —
lines.174: she is Tripura Sundari, her form the hue of vermilion, who, to those whose hearts harbour evil intent,
lines.175: and to deceivers, becomes terrifying, bending in her hand the curved mountain-bow;
lines.176: her body glows like fire — she who dwells as the red half of the Lord's own form.
lines.177: She is the pure one; she is the very auspiciousness of our Shankara's household;
lines.178: and to him she has also become mother; and because of this,
lines.179: she is the supreme goddess above all the gods;
lines.180: I shall not waver — I shall serve her, in true devotion, as if there were no other god at all.
lines.181: Have there ever been those who, without serving you, without worshipping your feet, resolutely followed only their own desire? There have —
lines.182: and if this servant of yours, having seen their example, does the same,
lines.183: is that deceit on my part, or is it itself a kind of penance?
lines.184: Even if I overstep, it is better that you bear with me than that you come, afterward, to hate me.
lines.185: That the great should still forgive their own devotees, even when those devotees act in ways worthy of hatred, is nothing new —
lines.186: it is your own nature — O golden one, united as the left half of him whose throat still darkens
lines.187: from the fresh poison he once drank!
lines.188: Even should I act in ways that provoke your anger, I shall go on praising you still.
lines.189: I have found the one true way to live; it is not a thing that lulls the mind into forgetting, nor one that dissolves under questioning;
lines.190: it does not reach even to the seven oceans or the eight great mountains, and yet, unreached,
lines.191: it lies at the very centre of the radiance that circles, day and night —
lines.193: Those who fix in their hearts, even for the blink of an eye, the fragrant green creeper who clings close
lines.194: to the radiant crescent-moon-crowned mountain of the Lord's matted hair, and thereby banish all their sorrows —
lines.195: will such people ever again be made to dwell
lines.196: in this hut of a body, soaked through with entrails, fat, and blood?
lines.197: When the soul that has taken up residence in this frail hut of a body draws near the boundary
lines.198: set for it by fierce Death, and wanders there in distress,
lines.199: may you come, surrounded by heavenly maidens as lovely as Urvashi, your bangled hand outstretched, and say 'fear not' —
lines.200: O Queen, who stands as music itself, strung upon the very nerves of this body!
lines.201: Nayaki, Naanmuki, Narayani, she who holds the five flower-arrows in her lotus hand,
lines.202: Saambhavi, Shankari, Shyamala, she who is the serpent-mouthed one,
lines.204: she who bears all these and other names — her refuge alone is our protection.
lines.205: The Lord who once, in righteous wrath, destroyed the strength of the graceless demons who thought only of wealth as their refuge,
lines.207: both stand crying 'refuge, refuge!' before the Queen; and her devotees,
lines.208: in this world, never again meet with death or rebirth.
lines.209: Land, horses, mighty elephants, the great crown, the palanquin,
lines.211: these are merely the outward signs granted to those who, even before all else, perform the penance
lines.212: of loving the lotus feet of the consort of the crescent-crowned Lord.
lines.213: Her slender waist bound with fine red silk; her full, high breasts strung with pearl necklaces;
lines.214: her hair, dense and dark, thick with jasmine; her three eyes —
lines.215: those who hold these in their heart and sit in solitude,
lines.216: no penance can compare to theirs.
lines.217: If, in your heart, you resolve that you will never again go begging in poverty to another and suffer humiliation, never again live in that instability —
lines.218: if you truly hold to that thought,
lines.219: then never, at any time, go near base men who have learned only never to learn;
lines.220: instead, take refuge at the everlasting feet of Tripurai.
lines.221: She who shines as a single form made of a thousand streaks of lightning,
lines.222: that Mother, Anandavalli, whose very heart is joy, who is at once the beginning,
lines.223: the middle everywhere, and the end of the rare Vedas —
lines.224: whether one meditates upon her or not, nothing at all is truly needed beyond her.
lines.225: Budding as one, unfolding into many, pervading this whole world,
lines.226: she stands; and yet she also stands apart, untouched by anything at all — within my own heart
lines.227: how she abides, imperishable, working still — who truly understands this mystery?
lines.228: Only he who once slept as a babe upon the banyan leaf, and my own Father, know it.
lines.229: I praise you, who with a mere two small measures save the whole universe through your righteous acts;
lines.230: and yet you have made me go before another,
lines.231: garland of fresh, sweet Tamil verse in hand, and speak both truth and falsehood there —
lines.232: is this, then, your true grace?
lines.233: She who dwells both in the red lotus and in the lotus of my own mind,
lines.234: the gracious woman with the youthful lotus-bosom, whose compassionate lotus-eyes,
lines.236: and lotus-feet — beyond these I have found no other refuge at all.
lines.237: I have never thought, considering the path of your austerity, 'there is no other refuge but this' —
lines.238: my mind has not truly dwelt there; you stand as one bow, five arrows, and a bowstring of sugarcane and flowers —
lines.239: and though the ignorant may not know it,
lines.240: even the children of your soft-footed devotees inherit your grace.
lines.241: O you whose speech is sweeter than milk! For your cool, great, flower-soft feet to rest,
lines.242: is my own head — the foul, doglike head of this servant of yours — truly less worthy
lines.243: than the head of Vishnu, or the crown of him before whom the gods bow, whose long matted locks bear the konrai flower,
lines.244: or the true pedestal on which the Vedas themselves stand and sing, even for a single day?
lines.245: Even a dog like me — you loved and came, treating me as if I were of worth,
lines.246: and you, of your own accord, without my even asking, claimed me as your own;
lines.247: you gave to this ghost-like fool the wisdom to know you as you truly are — what great fortune have I won!
lines.248: O Mother, O daughter of the mountain, O beloved younger sister of the red-eyed Vishnu!
lines.249: The red-limbed warrior who, with a golden bow, felled the three cities of the demons,
lines.250: and who wears the hide of the fierce, musk-eyed elephant-demon —
lines.251: the Queen who pressed her firm young breasts close against his very body,
lines.252: and the sugarcane bow and lotus flower in her red hand — these forever fill my thoughts.
lines.253: Giving some small proof, pointing toward the path that lies ahead,
lines.254: whatever a doctrine's teaching may be — like a peg driven into a hill, marking out one single faith —
lines.255: though they know well that she alone is the true Mistress underlying every one of these paths,
lines.256: it is only fools who go on proudly proclaiming that some other, separate faith exists.
lines.257: In vain I will not go to lesser gods who merely accept offerings, and clothe myself in excessive devotion to them;
lines.258: it is you alone I have chosen to love;
lines.259: apart from praising your glory, I will cherish nothing else, not for a single moment;
lines.260: and apart from the radiance of your sacred form, I see nothing — not this broad earth, not the four directions, not even the sky.
lines.261: Was it not through your own great power that the mighty ascetic, who once burned the bow-wielding Kama's body to ash before the very sky and all the worlds,
lines.262: came, through his union with you, to have broad arms and a red face,
lines.263: and a son who appeared as if born of ancient wisdom, with six faces and twelve arms —
lines.264: was this not, O Valli, entirely your own doing?
lines.265: I know no other power; I am small and lowly; I have no support at all
lines.266: except the tender red shoots that are your flower-feet — O you who sit enthroned beside the archer of the fresh golden mountain-bow!
lines.267: Even if the words I, a sinner, have woven together turn out worthless,
lines.268: they are still, in truth, hymns of praise to your sacred names.
lines.269: Those who never once, even for the flash of a lightning-instant, hold your form in mind — praise you, and bow to you though they might —
lines.270: such people, whatever their strength, lineage, family, learning, or virtue,
lines.271: will find those very things dwindle away, until they wander daily from hut to hut,
lines.272: begging bowl in hand, for their food — everywhere on this earth.
lines.273: Earth, water, fire, fierce wind, and the spreading sky; fragrance, taste, sound, form, and touch —
lines.274: all these come together as one in her, the Queen
lines.275: Sivakama Sundari; and those whose penance is to draw near her small feet —
lines.276: there is no wealth that such people do not possess.
lines.277: Wealth she gives, learning she gives, a mind never once known to falter she gives,
lines.278: a form fit for the gods she gives, kinship free of all deceit in the heart she gives,
lines.279: everything good she gives, to those called her devotees —
lines.280: such is the power of the glance from the corner of the eye of flower-haired Abirami.
lines.281: I have seen, to my eyes' delight, that beauty which the earth itself rejoices in —
lines.282: the melodious veena in her hand, her hand itself, her full breasts,
lines.283: and her dark-green hue, appearing born among the daughters of the fisherfolk race —
lines.284: the supreme beauty of our own Queen, in the kadamba forest.
lines.285: Valli, whose beauty none can equal, whose lotus feet have turned red
lines.286: from the long devotion of the six Vedas —
lines.287: while that tender branch, the dark Yamala Goddess, stands beside the young crescent moon on his sacred crown,
lines.288: why should you, O grieving heart, feel you have lost anything at all? Do not mourn — what lack could you possibly have?
lines.289: I stand and praise you now, that my own lacking might be ended; and should I be born again,
lines.290: whose fault would that be, if not your own? O slender-waisted one, whose waist, thin as a streak
lines.291: of lightning in the vast, long sky, seems ever on the verge of breaking —
lines.292: O lotus flower that our Lord has placed upon his matted crown, to end that very lack in you!
lines.293: Her garland is of kadamba flowers, her weapon the five flower-arrows, her bow of sugarcane;
lines.294: her hour of worship is the midnight watch when the Bhairavas praise her;
lines.295: her sacred feet are the very shelter she has set aside for us, her four red hands, her ruddy radiance —
lines.296: Mother, your name is Tripurai, and you have three eyes in one.
lines.297: The three-eyed Lord, the Vedas, Narayana, and Brahma —
lines.298: all praise her; and those who take the twin feet of Abirama Valli
lines.299: as their true reward, will dwell, while maidens dance and sing before them,
lines.300: upon golden couches in gardens of gold.
lines.301: Those who set their minds upon her sacred form —
lines.302: will dwell in the shade of the wish-granting tree; never again on this earth
lines.303: will they be lost, motherless, into faulty rebirth; from her navel-lotus once came forth
lines.304: the great mountains and the surging ocean and all fourteen worlds, she the fragrant, flower-haired one.
lines.305: I have fixed in my mind your entire form; and understanding your intent,
lines.306: I have blocked the very path by which Death approaches me directly;
lines.307: like a bee digging into a blossoming konrai flower, I have drawn out and taken into myself
lines.308: one whole portion of the Lord — O Bhairavi who wields the five flower-arrows!
lines.309: Bhairavi, Panchami, she who holds the noose and goad, she of the five flower-hands, she who to the wicked
lines.310: consumes their very life-breath as an offering — the great Chandi, Kali, the radiant, art-filled
lines.312: these are her sacred names, free of all blemish, that even the four Vedas themselves proclaim.
lines.313: Upon her sacred breasts, round and full like golden pitchers, anointed with fragrant sandal-paste —
lines.314: Abirama Valli, adorned with strands of pearl,
lines.315: with diamond earrings, and the rich corner-glance of her eyes,
lines.316: her red coral lips and moonlike face — all these I have painted, in these verses, for my own two eyes to behold.
lines.317: Even in her mere glance there is grace, for Abirama Valli; and we too have hearts willing to walk
lines.318: the path the Vedas themselves have shown; while that path lies open before them,
lines.319: what fellowship can there be, from now on, with those base men who instead spin round in blame,
lines.320: commit fierce sins, and sink into the wasted pit of hell?
lines.321: How she gathered me among her own devotees, how she drove away
lines.322: my cruel karma, how the fault in my own eye itself fled,
lines.323: how she revealed herself to me exactly as she truly is, so that my eyes and mind now rejoice at what they have seen —
lines.324: O divine one whose golden lotus feet dance — how she has made me dance too!
lines.325: O divine beauty! Since even the lesser gods of desire are but your own attendants,
lines.326: I will bow to no one else; in my heart I will praise no one else; with the deceitful
lines.327: I will keep no company; nor will I ever quarrel with those few who insist on saying 'this is mine, that is yours' —
lines.328: I have no wisdom of my own at all: it is entirely the great grace that your own eyes have placed in me.
lines.329: O divine one seated on the bee-filled lotus, in whose radiance the whole universe stands as mere light —
lines.330: whenever I dwell in my mind upon your shining sacred form,
lines.331: my inner faculties swell with rapture and overflow their banks,
lines.332: until I lose myself entirely — how, then, could I ever forget your wondrous ways?
lines.333: Those who, offering fresh, fragrant flowers, are able to bow morning and night before
lines.334: your fragrant lotus feet — feet which even all the unblinking gods themselves praise —
lines.335: such people come to possess the very seat of Indra, the elephant Airavata, the river Ganga,
lines.336: the thunderbolt weapon, and the wish-granting garden itself.
lines.337: She who wears a soft, red silken garment; she whose hair holds the shining red crescent moon;
lines.338: she who never enters the hearts of the deceitful; she whose waist is slender as a fine thread;
lines.339: she who is the very companion of our own Lord — from now on, watch, and you will see,
lines.340: she will never again create me for further birth, nor will she ever again need to create even you.
lines.341: In whatever direction one looks, one sees her noose and goad, and the five fresh flowers
lines.342: buzzing with cool-winged bees, and her sugarcane bow — she, Tripurai, who removes every one of my sorrows,
lines.343: her sacred body, her slender waist,
lines.344: her vermilion-anointed breasts, and the pearl necklace resting upon them — all these fill my sight.
lines.345: Her foot, which Vishnu, Brahma, the Vedas, and all the gods sought yet could not find, and her bangled hand —
lines.346: these, when I hold them before me, become a shielding boundary, a firm protection —
lines.347: so when fierce Death casts his glance upon me, come and stand visibly before me, I beg you;
lines.348: O you whose speech is cool and sweet as milk, honey, and refined sugar!
lines.349: Your sacred form, unreachable by speech or by thought, has yet made itself visible before my own eyes and even my own past deeds —
lines.350: and so the Lord who, with a single glance, once burned Kama to ash,
lines.351: now rules, holding you as one half of himself, in a manner that puts to shame the imperishable vow he once made, before the whole universe —
lines.353: I have come to you, taking you as my supreme refuge, even though I am but a lone, unworthy soul; among your own devotees,
lines.354: I ought not to be cast aside as 'unfit' —
lines.355: for I have taken refuge with him who once bent the mountain-bow to burn the enemies' three cities, and who cut off one of Brahma's heads with his own hand —
lines.356: O glorious one, who dwells as the left half of that very Lord!
lines.357: O radiant Lakshmi of the blooming lotus! So that your red feet may rest upon my head,
lines.358: may you, together with your consort who grants heaven itself,
lines.359: come and grant me that final, dreamless sleep beyond the fourth state, in which the bond between body and soul dissolves, and all awareness fades —
lines.360: may you both come before me, even should it cost you effort, in that very hour.
lines.361: So that I need suffer no more, she has come and entered the lotus of my own mind,
lines.362: and taken her seat there, as if it were her own ancient dwelling; and now, for me,
lines.363: there is nothing at all left wanting — O gentle one, who offers, as a feast
lines.364: to the sages who dwell in heaven, that very nectar the ocean of milk once yielded.
lines.365: She whose slender waist is fine as a streak of lightning, whom the wide-matted-locked Lord embraces;
lines.366: she whose soft breasts he clasps close, golden as they are —
lines.367: for those who, in turn, worship the devotees who worship her, praising her in exactly the manner the Vedas themselves prescribe,
lines.368: she grants a state in which they ride, amid the sounding of festival drums, upon the great white elephant.
lines.369: Melting in devotion, holding my mind fast at your feet, and living so as to please you always —
lines.370: in this manner you have claimed me as your servant; now I will never let my mind be bewildered
lines.371: by the pride of any other, nor will I ever walk the path such people walk —
lines.372: O you whose budding smile even the first three gods, and all others, praise!
lines.373: This much alone is laughable: that we should describe as 'young buds' the breasts of her who is Mother to this entire world;
lines.374: that we should speak of an 'ancient time' when she was born, O deer-eyed one — for she has no true beginning;
lines.375: that we should even call her 'daughter of the mountain' is itself a vain and empty word;
lines.376: indeed, for us to seek out and long to grasp her true nature at all is itself too great a thing to attempt.
lines.377: Devotees who worship her with longing find their eyes fill with tears, their bodies break out in gooseflesh,
lines.378: and, overflowing with a joy beyond measure, they lose their ordinary reason,
lines.379: grow intoxicated as if on sugarcane liquor, their speech stumbling —
lines.380: if this is what results, and they are called mad for it, then truly, the faith of Abirami is the best of all faiths.
lines.381: Whether good comes to me, or whether evil results, I myself understand nothing of it at all;
lines.382: everything is left to you; whatever I possess,
lines.383: I long ago gave up entirely, declaring it yours — O mountain of undying virtue,
lines.384: O ocean of grace, O gentle one born to the Himalaya!
lines.385: Komala Valli, who dwells in the lily-pond and the lotus-shrine;
lines.386: the dark Yamala Valli, who is free from all blemish; she of the indescribable
lines.387: dark-green body, mistress of every art, like a peacock in her grace —
lines.388: those who worship her to the very best of their ability become themselves the foremost lords of all the seven worlds.
lines.389: The Sun, the Moon, Fire, Kubera, Indra the king of the gods,
lines.390: Brahma seated in the lotus, the destroyer of the three cities, Krishna, the sage of the Podhigai hills,
lines.391: Kandha wielding the piercing spear, Ganapati, Kama, and others —
lines.392: countless are the meritorious beings who worship this young Goddess.
lines.393: Where did the fire that came to rest in the hand of Shankara, and the river that came to rest upon his head, go
lines.394: when he lovingly received and wore your lotus feet upon his crown?
lines.395: They found no place anywhere except in a heart that has truly arrived at love — never, at any time, in the false hearts
lines.396: of the fickle; O innocent, beautiful cuckoo, unskilled in guile!
lines.397: In the kadamba forest she dwells as a cuckoo; in the vast and beautiful Himalayan mountains
lines.398: she dwells as a graceful peacock; in the sky she dwells as the risen sunlight;
lines.399: upon the lotus she dwells as the swan —
lines.400: she who is the heavy-eardropped bride the Himalaya once gave in marriage to the Lord of Kailasa.
lines.401: Kongai Valli, whose fragrant breasts rival the konrai garland that embraces her earrings,
lines.402: her sacred, tall shoulders that rival the bamboo, and her sugarcane bow,
lines.403: her mighty, fragrant flower-arrows that vie to be desired, and her white smile,
lines.404: and her eyes that rival the doe's — these forever rise within my heart.
lines.405: She who is our own true mother, our Abirama Valli, who brought the entire universe
lines.406: into bloom, whose hue is that of the pomegranate flower;
lines.407: she who protects this whole earth, who holds in her hand the noose and goad, together with the sugarcane bow,
lines.408: she of the three eyes — no harm whatsoever can ever come to those who worship her.
